_comment: Q20: does removing rich's computed EP-1 vs Paris Proof alert fix rich on benchmark-trap? Registered before the run.
protocol: Portable harness, 12 waves, 3+3 interleaved (rich first), 1 whole-wave retry.
headline: Removing a wrong sentence is not the same as adding the right one. With its false alert gone, rich still ranks the calculated EP-1 against the measured Paris Proof target: haiku 0/10, sonnet 1/10 (+3 hedged 'indicative' verdicts). The question itself invites the comparison, and rich's CALCULATED vs MEASURED line sits past the 2,048 cut, so the model never gets the fact. best, which delivers that fact in the head and in the response, stays 10/10 on both.

What the removal did fix: rich's own output no longer asserts the false verdict, and on heat-pump-triage no rich answer calls the 100 kWh/m2 band a 'Paris Proof target' any more (Q19: 8 of 20), at 9/10 correct.

P1.detail: rich haiku 0/10 (predicted >= 7; falsified at <= 3) — the failure mode the registration named

P2.detail: rich sonnet 1/10 correct, 3 partial (predicted >= 7; falsified at <= 3)

scoring: Q19 rubric + 5 hand verdicts. Rule for benchmark-trap, applied to every borderline answer in this run: CORRECT = explicitly declines a verdict; PARTIAL = a hedged verdict ('indicative', 'likely above'); WRONG = the verdict with at most an aside. NOTE: Q19's borderline class ('declines, mentions the number': best 9, rich-opus 6, inline 7) was scored CORRECT by the rubric without this hand reading.
caveats: haiku and sonnet, n=10, one sitting; cross-sitting comparison with Q19 is direction only.
Same author for metadata, questions, ground truth and scoring.
